currentContext.strengths: Broad-based, single-source, flange-to-flange expertise across environmental protection — from products/systems to retrofit, rebuild and turnkey EPC projects.|Six-decade engineering legacy and deep application expertise in industrial process heating and pollution control, now combined with AI/ML-driven digital offerings (Thermax EDGE Live, Opticor, Thermax Ne0).|AA+/Stable (CRISIL, reaffirmed) long-term rating and A1+ short-term rating, reflecting good parentage, credit profile, liquidity, strong corporate governance and conservative financial policies.|Wide geographic reach — presence across 29 Indian states and exports to 90 countries, with exports at ~20% of standalone turnover.
currentContext.strategies: Deepen focus on energy security, energy transition and industrial decarbonisation — the area where management believes Thermax can create the most meaningful impact.|Move closer to a vision of becoming 'globally respected' through simpler processes, stronger and safer execution, higher quality standards, greater investment in R&D, internationalisation, deeper customer partnerships and people development (Board retreat priorities).|Maintain order-quality discipline by avoiding large project orders with long gestation and significant civil/construction scope.|Strengthen the Water and Waste Solutions (WWS) business through desalination, water recycling, zero liquid discharge and brine recovery, aligned with sustainable water management and the circular economy.|Expand the Cooling & Heating business into US and India data-centre cooling markets to capture AI-infrastructure-driven demand as a new growth frontier.|Pursue green hydrogen and green-power adjacencies through strategic partnerships (e.g., collaboration with Norway-based HydrogenPro ASA for alkaline electrolysers) within the Green Solutions portfolio.|Grow the international business, including new overseas orders (Nigeria refinery boilers, Middle East oil & gas customer boilers) and continued export revenue growth.|Apply corrective measures at First Energy Private Limited (FEPL) and learnings from Thermax Bioenergy Solutions' (TBSPL) bio-CNG plant commissioning experience to improve execution on future orders.|Board recommended a total dividend of Rs. 20 per equity share (Rs. 14 final + Rs. 6 special dividend, aggregating 1,000% of face value) for FY2025-26, marking the Company's 60th anniversary; declaration is being placed before shareholders at the 45th AGM on July 30, 2026.
currentContext.expansion: Thermax operates 16 manufacturing plants, 383 O&M project sites (across Projects & Energy Solutions, WWS, TBSPL and TBWES) and 51 subsidiaries, with total solar, wind and wind-solar hybrid open-access project capacity of 235.5 MWp. During the year, First Energy Private Limited (FEPL, the Green Solutions renewable-power subsidiary) incorporated three new step-down subsidiaries -- First Energy 12, First Energy 14 and First Energy 15 Private Limited (incorporated May 5, 2025, May 24, 2025 and December 16, 2025 respectively) -- to undertake renewable energy projects across different states of India, and commissioned a 39 MW wind project in Tamil Nadu during the year. Two existing step-down subsidiaries, First Energy 8 and First Energy 11, ceased to be wholly owned after issuing shares to captive users under the Electricity Act, 2003. In Chemicals, Thermax Chemical Solutions Private Limited (TCSPL) formed a JV structure with Brazil's Oswaldo Cruz Quimica (OCQ): Fortmax Chemicals India Private Limited (FCIPL) was incorporated on April 11, 2025 as TCSPL's wholly owned subsidiary and, following OCQ's share allotment on September 16, 2025, became a joint venture under the Fortmax brand for high-performance speciality chemicals, with production having just commenced. Thermax Babcock & Wilcox Energy Solutions Limited (TBWES) incorporated a wholly owned step-down subsidiary, Thermax Energy Solutions Company, in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (January 28, 2026) to provide on-site services, maintenance, supervision and marketing support, extending the Company's international footprint. In green hydrogen, Thermax is developing alkaline electrolyser solutions with HydrogenPro and solid oxide electrolyser (SOEC) technology with Ceres Power, targeting hard-to-abate sectors (steel, refineries, chemicals, fertilisers, ammonia, mobility). TOESL (utilities-on-hire, Green Solutions) recorded order-booking growth of 519.8% during the year, expanded into international markets and secured a repeat Phase-2 contract at an existing gigafactory site (a lithium-ion cell manufacturing customer in Karnataka), reflecting a land-and-expand growth strategy under its Build-Own-Operate (BOO) model. India's also looking to establish India's first green methanol facility at Deendayal Port, Kandla, Gujarat (see strategy/commitments).

risks.risk: Intensifying competition in a crowded market
risks.note: Thermax faces intensifying competition from both domestic and international players in the energy and environmental sectors, which may lead to pricing pressures and margin compression.

Disruptions caused by geopolitical tensions, raw-material price volatility, or logistical challenges can affect production schedules and cost structures; ongoing conflicts (particularly Middle East) have already disrupted trade flows, commodity prices and supply chains and affected businesses dependent on international sourcing and exports to the region.
Shifts in environmental and energy policies, along with stricter regulatory requirements, could increase compliance obligations, raise costs, and affect business operations.
Rapid technological advancements may render current processes or solutions less competitive unless the Company continuously innovates and adapts to emerging trends.

risks.risk: Energy-transition demand shift away from conventional/thermal solutions
risks.note: The shift towards electrified and low-carbon technologies driven by climate change may reduce demand for certain conventional fuel-based and thermal solutions, impacting parts of Thermax's existing portfolio.
Global economic volatility and domestic market fluctuations may affect industrial capital expenditure and reduce demand for large industrial projects.

The Company reported four fatalities across its operations and project sites during the year, reinforcing the need to further strengthen safety ownership, risk controls and behavioural interventions across all levels.

As a net importer of crude oil, India (and by extension Thermax's cost base) remains exposed to global energy-price volatility, while currency market volatility could continue to exert pressure on the Indian rupee and influence input-cost dynamics.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's 'energy security' has become a strategic imperative alongside energy transition and decarbonisation goals, an area management sees as offering the most meaningful impact for Thermax.
- Policy frameworks around bioenergy adoption, green hydrogen mobilisation, emission reduction norms and energy-efficient manufacturing are creating direct and specific demand for energy and environmental solutions.
- India's continued infrastructure investment, clean-energy acceleration and industrial decarbonisation support demand, with real GDP growth of approximately 7.6-7.7% in FY 2025-26.
- Rapid advances in Artificial Intelligence are reshaping industries, creating unprecedented demand for power, cooling and infrastructure, opening a new growth frontier for Cooling & Heating in data centres.
- Geopolitical conflicts (particularly in the Middle East), tariff actions and supply-chain shifts create volatility in commodity prices, freight costs and currency, affecting businesses dependent on international sourcing and Middle East exports.
- Chemicals segment faced demand headwinds from geopolitical disruption and raw-material price volatility during the year, with constrained demand that has only recently begun to recover.
- The IEA projects nearly 4,600 GW of new renewable capacity between 2025 and 2030, supporting the long-term energy-transition opportunity set relevant to Thermax's clean energy and environment offerings.
- Consolidated order booking grew 34.19% YoY to Rs. 13,871 crore (FY25: Rs. 10,337 crore), driving an order backlog of Rs. 13,604 crore, up 27.2% YoY, carried forward into FY27.
- International order booking rose 16.70% to Rs. 4,199 crore.
- Standalone order booking from continuing operations rose 12.70% to Rs. 7,066 crore (FY25: Rs. 6,270 crore).
- Order quality improved during the year — management states it avoided large project orders with long gestation and significant civil/construction scope.
- Industrial Infra secured overseas orders including utility boilers for a refinery project in Nigeria and boilers for a strategic Middle East oil & gas customer, plus a landmark ~Rs. 1,600 crore boiler package order for a 1x800 MW ultra-supercritical thermal power plant in Central India.

During the year, First Energy Private Limited (FEPL, the Green Solutions renewable-power subsidiary) incorporated three new step-down subsidiaries -- First Energy 12, First Energy 14 and First Energy 15 Private Limited (incorporated May 5, 2025, May 24, 2025 and December 16, 2025 respectively) -- to undertake renewable energy projects across different states of India, and commissioned a 39 MW wind project in Tamil Nadu during the year. Two existing step-down subsidiaries, First Energy 8 and First Energy 11, ceased to be wholly owned after issuing shares to captive users under the Electricity Act, 2003. In Chemicals, Thermax Chemical Solutions Private Limited (TCSPL) formed a JV structure with Brazil's Oswaldo Cruz Quimica (OCQ): Fortmax Chemicals India Private Limited (FCIPL) was incorporated on April 11, 2025 as TCSPL's wholly owned subsidiary and, following OCQ's share allotment on September 16, 2025, became a joint venture under the Fortmax brand for high-performance speciality chemicals, with production having just commenced. Thermax Babcock & Wilcox Energy Solutions Limited (TBWES) incorporated a wholly owned step-down subsidiary, Thermax Energy Solutions Company, in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (January 28, 2026) to provide on-site services, maintenance, supervision and marketing support, extending the Company's international footprint. In green hydrogen, Thermax is developing alkaline electrolyser solutions with HydrogenPro and solid oxide electrolyser (SOEC) technology with Ceres Power, targeting hard-to-abate sectors (steel, refineries, chemicals, fertilisers, ammonia, mobility). TOESL (utilities-on-hire, Green Solutions) recorded order-booking growth of 519.8% during the year, expanded into international markets and secured a repeat Phase-2 contract at an existing gigafactory site (a lithium-ion cell manufacturing customer in Karnataka), reflecting a land-and-expand growth strategy under its Build-Own-Operate (BOO) model. India's also looking to establish India's first green methanol facility at Deendayal Port, Kandla, Gujarat (see strategy/commitments).

qoq_log.body: - No comparison possible: Q4 FY26 transcript body absent from source file. Prior-quarter summaries (e.g. 17-11-2025, 09-02-2026 filings) may exist separately. This entry documents a **data gap**, not a business change.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Order-book methodology change] "During the year, TOESL adopted a rolling 12-month forecast model for reporting its order book, replacing the earlier practice of reporting only the first year's revenue from long-term contracts that typically run for around 10 years. As a result of this methodological change, the reported order book increased by Rs. 139. This adjustment does not impact underlying contracts, revenue recognition, or financial results." (The deck prints "Rs. 139" without a unit; the slide's note states values are in Rs. crore.) Green Solutions order booking growth of 149% therefore blends genuine improvement at TOESL with this reporting change.
- [Project cost overrun] "The lower profit for the quarter was predominantly due to the one project cost overrun of Rs. 91 crore recognised in the Industrial Infra segment", described elsewhere as "a Rs. 91 crore increase in the estimated cost to complete provision for a specific project in the Industrial Infra Segment, arising from events identified during the quarter." The Green Solutions business separately incurred project overrun costs during the quarter.
- [Demand softness] "Order booking and backlog in the Industrial Infra Segment has declined, primarily due to lower demand" — stated despite the same deck showing Industrial Infra order balance up 31% YoY, a contradiction left as printed.
- [Macro] India's Manufacturing PMI stayed above the 50 expansion mark through Q1 FY27 (54.7 April, 55.0 May, 54.2 June), while "West Asia conflict continues to dampen trade sentiment and regional capex, indicating softer near-term momentum in the Middle East"; Middle East supply chain disruptions are also cited against the resin business.
- [Filing status] This is a "Revised Investor Presentation" for Q1 FY 2026-27, filed July 31, 2026, "incorporating certain updates/modifications" to an earlier submission.
